source_text:
Exercise 6.3 — Returnability on a five-state chain
      
      
        States $s_1,\dots,s_5$ with deterministic transitions: $s_1\to\{s_1,s_2\}$, $s_2\to\{s_1,s_3\}$, $s_3\to\{s_2,s_4\}$, $s_4\to\{s_3,s_5\}$, $s_5\to\{s_5\}$ (a trap). Suppose the previous ergodic set is $\hat S_{t-1}=\{s_1,s_2\}$ and the GP has certified all five states, $S_t=\{s_1,\dots,s_5\}$. Compute $R^{\rm reach}(\hat S_{t-1})$, $R^{\rm ret}_n(S_t,\hat S_{t-1})$ for $n=1,2,3$, the closure $\bar R^{\rm ret}$, and $\hat S_t$. Which certified-safe state is never explored, and why is that the right answer? What changes if $s_5$ gets an action back to $s_4$?
        
          Show answer
          
            $R^{\rm reach}(\{s_1,s_2\})=\{s_1,s_2\}\cup\{f(s',a)\}=\{s_1,s_2,s_3\}$ (from $s_2$ one reaches $s_3$; $s_1$ and $s_2$ reach each other).
            Returnability, target $\bar S=\{s_1,s_2\}$, passing through $S_t$: $R^{\rm ret}_1=\{s_1,s_2\}\cup\{s\in S_t:\exists a,\ f(s,a)\in\{s_1,s_2\}\}=\{s_1,s_2,s_3\}$ (only $s_3\to s_2$ enters the target). $R^{\rm ret}_2=R^{\rm ret}(S_t,\{s_1,s_2,s_3\})=\{s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4\}$ ($s_4\to s_3$). $R^{\rm ret}_3$: does any remaining state reach $\{s_1,\dots,s_4\}$? $s_5$ only reaches itself, so $R^{\rm ret}_3=R^{\rm ret}_2$ and the closure is $\bar R^{\rm ret}(S_t,\hat S_{t-1})=\{s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4\}$.
            $\hat S_t=\{s\in S_t:\ s\in R^{\rm reach}(\hat S_{t-1})\cap\bar R^{\rm ret}\}=\{s_1,s_2,s_3\}\cap\{s_1,\dots,s_4\}=\{s_1,s_2,s_3\}$. State $s_4$ is returnable but not yet reachable in one step from the old ergodic set; it enters $\hat S_{t+1}$ once $s_3$ is ergodic. State $s_5$ is certified above the threshold but is a trap: visiting it would force the agent to stay there forever, so no returning path exists and it is (correctly) never explored, however safe its feature value. If $s_5$ gains an action to $s_4$, then $R^{\rm ret}_3$ picks it up and the closure becomes all five states; $s_5$ becomes explorable as soon as it is one-step reachable from the ergodic set.
